- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to recent history.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; dampen forecast peaks and avoid sharp upward revisions.
- After a price spike (e.g., >72.0), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to subsequent forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizons; if forecast is >73.0, reduce by 0.5–1.5 points unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows a single positive signal (e.g., 0.20), model may overfit to that signal; cap forecast increases to 1–2% above recent mean unless confirmed by multiple signals.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day window; apply a 0.5–1.0 point downward bias to early forecast days if sentiment is flat.
